title: IFGL Refractories Ltd - 540774 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IFGL Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 276 crore and FY26 consolidated income grew 14% to INR 1,904 crore; consolidated Q4 EBITDA margin 8.6%.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income was INR 278 crore (+2% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 11.8%, while FY26 standalone EBITDA margin was 11.3%. Domestic revenue grew 7% YoY in Q4 and 20% for FY26 to INR 864 crore, but exports fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical and market headwinds. Margins were hit by product mix shifts, lower exports and higher raw material and freight costs. Management also announced a senior leadership reshuffle, with Mukesh Rawal moving to India operations and Manoj Rakhecha to international operations.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2.15 per share (21.5% of face value)

segments.name: Domestic (India)
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue reached INR 864 crore, up 7% YoY in Q4 and 20% for FY26. Management says growth comes from share gains in large integrated steel plants and new small foundry accounts; it does not split the growth by source.

segments.name: Exports (India-made)
segments.commentary: Export revenue fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical and external market headwinds. Management says volumes have started to improve, and it has added manpower to rebuild export accounts.

segments.name: USA (Americas)
segments.commentary: US revenue grew 26% YoY in Q4 and 25% in FY26, with subsidiary EBITDA margins back in the high-teens (described later as double-digit). Management calls the margins sustainable.

segments.name: Sheffield Refractories (UK)
segments.commentary: Management reports strong performance with healthy growth, operating leverage and sustained customer demand. Phase 1 of the India technology transfer is complete.

segments.name: Hofmann Ceramics (Germany)
segments.commentary: Losses fell significantly in FY26 after turnaround steps and cost cuts. Management expects the business to move close to breakeven during FY27.

segments.name: Monocon (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue recovered despite losing a key high-margin UK customer after a plant closure. Management targets breakeven by Q4 FY27 and is entering foundry and new geographies.

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting double-digit domestic volume growth in FY27, and says it expects to grow well above underlying market growth over the medium term.
Management expects US results to show major growth in FY27 and expects the Americas to remain an important contributor.
Hofmann is expected to move close to breakeven during FY27; Monocon is targeted to reach breakeven by Q4 FY27.
Management is in talks with customers on price revisions and expects a reasonable pass-through of cost increases.
The Sheffield plastic ramming technology is expected to be ready for full-fledged market entry by end of CY2026, after trials.
Consolidated amortisation of about INR 26.7 crore a year ends from FY27 because the legacy goodwill from the 2017 amalgamation is fully amortised.
capex_capacity: Greenfield project in Khurda, Odisha: work has picked up, but the Board is still evaluating pace and structure, with no timeline given.
Gujarat (Bhachau) greenfield plant: awaiting statutory approvals from the Government of India under Press Note 3; no timeline given.
Vizag plant: first energy optimizing furnace (EOF) campaign completed with a lining and tuyere blocks made in-house, exceeding 1,000 heats.
Management says recent capex in Vizag, Rourkela and R&D will mature and generate returns; capex is described as under control.
Alumina and basic brick capacity for cement is planned at Bhachau and a joint venture basic brick line is coming up.
demand_pricing: Indian steel capacity expansion announcements are expected to drive refractory demand; management says customers increasingly prefer full-range refractory solution providers.
Raw material costs remain elevated due to energy, freight and currency; imported minerals and shipping rates are the key cost swing factors.
Competitive pricing has been accepted in bricks and casting flux to win new accounts, with margins initially lean.
Early FY27 saw LPG availability issues linked to West Asia developments.
Europe: order books are improving, with policy support for domestic manufacturing, defence and infrastructure. German foundries serving specialised alloys are on an uptrend.
Monocon has raised prices where input and logistics costs require, and says customers are accepting this.

qa_highlights.question: What operational triggers will reverse the five-year decline in return metrics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said market conditions have changed and pointed to the US turnaround and Hofmann/Monocon fixes, with results expected within a year. It also said recent capex will mature and generate returns.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital expanded, and what is the plan for inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said working capital cycle has reduced versus last year and cash was generated from it, and that inventory is on a declining trend. No quantified inventory days were given.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital deployment be balanced against rising net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said debt is negligible, that investment in Vizag, Rourkela and R&D is for future returns, and that capex is under control. Consolidated debt is INR 195.6 crore against cash of INR 122 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Sheffield technology transfer add to top line, and what is the delta?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukesh Rawal said the customer base is identified, equipment is online and trial orders are in hand, with full market entry expected by end of CY2026. He said the revenue delta would be provided later by the CFO. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US demand outlook for Q1 FY27 and for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects major US growth in FY27, with new customer trials succeeding. Mexico is growing and foundry business is being added in the US and Mexico.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic volume growth target 15-20% for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is at least targeting double-digit domestic growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Monocon's turnaround and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Monocon is entering new geographies and products, including foundries, with trials underway. Management aims to restore profitability by Q4 FY27 and is seeking price hikes where needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are exports underwhelming, and is it a deliberate pullback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift to India was a deliberate decision because global steel is shrinking, and it will retarget exports as opportunities arise. Geopolitical factors and European plant closures were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving senior management exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Mihir Bajoria said the exits are normal churn after the former CEO, Mr. Arasu, left with his team. Mukesh Rawal said the top team is restructured and in place, and he returns full-time from August.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from product mix, lower exports, and raw material and shipping cost swings; price pass-through is still under negotiation.
Leadership transition: former CEO and senior team exits, with Mukesh Rawal full-time from August and Manoj Rakhecha moving to international operations.
Export volumes fell 11% in FY26 and export accounts may need rebuilding.
Hofmann and Monocon are still loss-making, with breakeven targets for FY27 and Q4 FY27.
Working capital and inventory levels are high, and consolidated net debt has emerged versus earlier cash-rich position.
Ongoing ambiguity over Khurda and Gujarat greenfield timing, pending government approvals.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic share gains and the US business, but cautious on exports, Europe and Monocon. Evasive on capex timing (Khurda and Gujarat greenfield) and on exact revenue deltas, and defensive on leadership churn.
key_quotes: Importantly, these appointments represent continuity rather than change.
I'm pleased to share that Phase 1 has been successfully completed, including product recipe transfer, knowledge sharing and joint product development activities.
So, I am a very firm believer that the numbers what we have presented for US are not one -off, but those would be sustainable quarter-on-quarter, you know.

adds.what: Greenfield plant in Khurda, Odisha (no capacity or timeline given; Board still evaluating pace and structure)
Gujarat (Bhachau) greenfield plant, awaiting Press Note 3 statutory approvals (no timeline)

growth.why: Management targets at least double-digit domestic volume growth in FY27 and major US growth, backed by share gains and new foundry accounts but no specific capacity, orders or contracts; the Khurda and Bhachau greenfield plants have no timelines and capex is deferred, so growth backing is partial at best.

mgmt.note: Senior leadership reshuffle announced on the call: Mukesh Rawal moves to India operations and Manoj Rakhecha to international operations; no stated growth plan for the new roles.
